title: Big time: synchronous convergent evolution of giant body size in European earthworms (Crassiclitellata: Lumbricidae, Hormogastridae) and putative evolutionary pressures
content:
Abstract
European giant earthworms (Crassiclitellata, Lumbricoidea) exhibit remarkable convergent evolution, yet the drivers of this radiation remain poorly characterized. Using Anchored Hybrid Enrichment (660 loci, 72 species), we reconstructed a time-calibrated phylogeny for giant lineages within Lumbricidae and Hormogastridae to investigate the tempo of the evolution of large body size and its correlation with environmental variables. Results showed that large size in Hormogastridae evolved earlier and remained more stable than in Lumbricidae, potentially explaining their lower species richness and restricted geographic ranges. Divergence time estimates indicated that gigantism within Lumbricoidea emerged synchronically across different genera around the Middle Miocene Climate Optimum and Transition (17–14 Mya). As no correlation between past climatic variables and body size was detected, those global climate shifts likely influenced body size indirectly through the expansion of deciduous forests and open grasslands. Significant correlations with current environmental variables suggested the existence of two distinct adaptive peaks, where larger body sizes are promoted by both stable oceanic-like and Mediterranean-like climates. However, the high percentage of unexplained variance indicated that environmental factors alone are insufficient to explain large body size distribution. Improved phylogenetic resolution highlighted necessary systematic changes, including the establishment of Neoctolasion gen. nov.
